rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice when spot means see or notice something.

example.english: I can spot you waiting at the door.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gin3 dou2 nei5 hai2 mun4 hau2 dang2 gan2

rows.note: Use this when spot means find or locate something rather than merely see it.

example.english: I finally managed to spot the book.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 jyu1 wan2 dou2 bun2 syu1 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a place or location, rather than a mark on a surface.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 dei6 fong1 hou2 fong1 bin6

rows.note: Use this for a stain or dirty mark that you want to remove.

example.english: The shirt has a spot that won't wash out.
example.traditional: 件衫有污漬，點都洗唔甩。
example.jyutping: gin6 saam1 jau5 wu1 zik1 dim2 dou1 sai2 m4 lat1

rows.note: Use this for a naturally occurring colored patch or spot on an animal, plant, or object.

example.english: This butterfly has a beautiful spot.
example.traditional: 呢隻蝴蝶有一個好靚嘅斑點。
example.jyutping: ni1 zek3 wu4 dip6 jau5 jat1 go3 hou2 leng3 ge3 baan1 dim2

rows.note: Use this when something stains or makes a surface visibly dirty.

example.english: Your ink has left a spot on the table.
example.traditional: 你啲墨水整污糟張枱喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 di1 mak6 seoi2 zing2 wu1 zou1 zoeng1 toi2 laa3

rows.note: Use this specifically for a pimple or acne spot, rather than a general mark or stain.

example.english: I have a spot on my forehead.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ngaak6 tau4 saang1 zo2 nap1 am3 cong1

rows.jyutping: zing2 dou3 A jat1 taat3 taat3
rows.note: Use this construction when making an object blotchy or covered all over with spots, not for leaving just one stain.

example.english: You’ve left spot after spot all over the table.
example.traditional: 張枱畀你整到一撻撻喇。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 toi2 bei2 nei5 zing2 dou3 jat1 taat3 taat3 laa3
